subject: READ statement
notes: NOW (kb/Work PB3334, INDEXED on the keyed store engine): the INDEXED organization moved to the keyed store engine (kb/Work PB3334; DESIGN-runtime-library 2.2.1.4): the duplicate order is the alternate tree's (key, release ordinal) order, the ordinal minted from the meta page's release mint; the record list, its sort and its whole-store framing went with the whole store. kb/Work PB341 LANDED. RULE: 'For an indexed file being sequentially accessed, records having the same duplicate value in an alternate record key that is the key of reference are made available in the same order, or, in the case of PREVIOUS, in the reverse order, in which they are released by execution of WRITE statements, or by execution of REWRITE statements that create such duplicate values.' VALIDATED: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "records having the same duplicate value in an alternate record key that is the key of reference are made available in the same order" -> OK 26). WAS DIVERGES: IndexedStore.Release carried ONE Arrival for the whole record and IndexedConnector.Rewrite collapsed its per-key loop into one altChanged bool, so a REWRITE that changed ANY alternate key repositioned the record last in the duplicate set of EVERY alternate key - contrary to 14.9.35.4 GR24 a) ('When the value of a specific alternate record key is not changed, the order of retrieval when that key is the key of reference remains unchanged', --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)). MEASURED before the fix (probe pb341a.cob: 01/AA/PP and 02/AA/PP released in that order, then REWRITE of 01 changing only R-A1): the R-A2 walk answered 02 then 01. NOW: IndexedStore.Release.Ordinals is a VECTOR - slot 0 the prime key, slot i+1 the i-th alternate; Write stamps one fresh ordinal into every slot (the record is released under every key at once, 14.9.51.4 GR40); Rewrite re-stamps ONLY the keys whose value or SUPPRESS WHEN state actually changed, and the changed test is KeyEq under the key's collating sequence per GR24's closing sentence ('The comparison used for determining changes to the key is based on the collating sequence for the file according to the rules for a relation condition', --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); IndexedConnector.SelectSequentialRecord(keyIndex) ties on THAT key's ordinal; PersistOrder writes the physical file in a topological order of the per-key duplicate orders so a reload - which can only give every key the file's own order - reproduces all of them. PINNED: conformance:cases/9.1.13.2-Successful-completion/l1_rewrite_alt_key_order legs B and C (an untouched R-A2 keeps 01,02,03 while the changed R-A1 moves the record last in its new set) and leg D (both orders survive CLOSE/OPEN); the forward and reverse duplicate walks are pinned by conformance:cases/9.1.13.2-Successful-completion/l1_read_alt_dup_walk and conformance:cases/14.9.30-READ/l1_start_dup_set_entry. RESIDUE (a NEW, separate defect, not this rule's): the per-key orders can be made mutually CYCLIC by a REWRITE that moves one record into another's duplicate set under key A while both stay duplicates under key B, and no single sequence of record images can then carry both orders across a CLOSE - the physical framing has one order and the model has one per key. PersistOrder appends the cyclic residue in release order, which loses one key's repositioning. || kb/Work PB2693 (w1045d): the release ordinals are PERSISTED with each record and the release mint in the store header (store format 4), so every key's duplicate order survives a CLOSE/OPEN even when no single record order carries them all (the PB701 cyclic residue is gone), and a coherent reload after another run unit's DELETE no longer renumbers them, which made a duplicate walk skip a record. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/IndexedConnector.cs#PersistOrder (kb/Work PB2693 deleted the topological persist order: each record's release ordinals are persisted with it (store format 4), so the file order decides nothing) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/IndexedConnector.cs#Ordered (the INDEXED organization moved to the keyed store engine (kb/Work PB3334;
